  Meeting Rules and Regulation

Section 2.24.060 of the Alhambra Municipal Code provides for the Planning Commission to establish
and enforce its own rules and regulations for its meetings. The Planning Commission uses those rules
and regulations established by the Municipal Code and implemented for use by the City Council.

Addressing the Commission:

In person: Any person wishing to address the Commission during the meeting is asked to complete a
Speaker Request Card and submit it to the Secretary. When called upon by the President, please step
to the podium and give your name, address and organization or other party you represent, if any, in an
audible tone of voice for the record.

Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the “Raise
Hand” function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will unmute speakers
participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your time to speak.

Comments are limited to 5 minutes; however, the presiding officer may either extend or reduce the
maximum time to such period of time as the Commission may determine.

All comments shall be addressed to the Commission as a body and not to any member thereof. No
person, other than the Commission and the person having the floor, shall be permitted to enter into any
discussion, either directly or through a member of the Commission, without the permission of the
President. No question shall be asked a Commissioner except through the President.

Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated should
email or call the Community Development Department at mmccurley@alhambraca.gov or (626) 570-
5034. All requests for accommodations or translation services shall be made by 4 p.m. the Thursday

prior to the Planning Commission meeting. If accommodation or translation is not requested by 4 p.m.
the Thursday prior to the Planning Commission meeting, staff will try to accommodate the request to
the best of their efforts to provide as much accessibility as possible while also maintaining public safety.
All participants are encouraged to email their comments prior to the beginning of the meeting, but are
not required to do so. All written comments received prior to the meeting will be entered into the record
and distributed to the Planning Commission for their review.

Standards of Decorum: Any person addressing the Commission who refuses to stop speaking after
his/her time has expired or any person who behaves in such a manner as to interfere with or impede
the progress of the Planning Commission meeting who, after a request by the President, refuses to
cease such behavior may be muted or barred from the meeting upon direction of the President.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or his/her designee, may be Sergeant-at-Arms of the
Commission meetings. If present, the Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given
by the President for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the Commission meeting.

Persons Authorized to be Within Rail: No person, except City officials, their representatives, and
newspaper reporters, shall be permitted within the rail in front of the Council Chamber without the
express consent of the Commission.

PROPOSAL:
This is an application for a Conditional Use Permit CUP-24-04 to allow the operation of Comfort
Paradise Training Institute, a vocational school for nurses and nursing assistants, within an
existing 625 square foot commercial tenant space located at 1227 West Valley Boulevard, Unit
117, in the CMU (Commercial Mixed-Use) zone.

LOCATION:
The site is located on the north side of West Valley Boulevard, mid-block between South
Marguerita Avenue and Edith Avenue. The site is approximately 39,776 square feet and is
developed with a two-story commercial building, known as “World Plaza”, built in 1985. Since its
development, the building has been occupied by various office and commercial uses. The site is
located within the CMU (Commercial Mixed-Use) zone in an area featuring a variety of commercial
and office uses. The surrounding properties to the north are zoned RH (Residential High Density)
and the properties to the east, south, and west are zoned CMU (Commercial Mixed-Use).

ANALYSIS:
Conditional Use Permit

The Applicant is requesting approval of a Conditional Use Permit to allow a vocational school
within a 625 square foot first-floor unit of an existing commercial building, located at 1227 West
Valley Boulevard, Unit 117. Pursuant to AMC Section 23.05.020, Colleges and Trade Schools
are a conditionally permitted use in the CMU (Commercial Mixed-Use) zone subject to approval
of a Conditional Use Permit by the Planning Commission. AMC Section 23.35.020 defines
Colleges and Trade Schools as: “Institutions of higher education primarily for adults providing
curricula of a general, religious, or professional nature, granting degrees or professional
certifications and including junior colleges, business and computer schools, management training,
and technical and trade schools. This classification excludes Instructional Services such as music
lessons.” The proposed Comfort Paradise Training Institute vocational nursing school, if approved
by the Planning Commission, would provide vocational nursing educational services, which will
be easily accessible to nearby residents, and which would add to the diversity of businesses
offered in the area. The proposed use would also help further General Plan Goal QL-10C to
“Promote education that teaches skills that match local job opportunities.”

Comfort Paradise Training Institute has been in business at this location since 2022, operating as
an office space. This is the business’ only location and they are proposing to expand their existing
operation by providing education and training to students seeking certification in nursing
assistance and vocational nursing. The business is accredited by the California Department of

training. The subject tenant space is already used as an office space to provide the theoretical
portion of the training over Zoom. The proposed incorporation of on-site, in-person instruction will
allow students to practice on and train with anatomical models and nursing lab equipment in a
classroom setting. No “hands-on” clinical training with patients will occur on-site, nor will any
patients be treated on-site. The vocational school partners with local hospitals and clinics for
hands-on clinical training that occurs off-site in various settings such as hospitals, nursing homes,
and rehabilitation centers. Comfort Paradise Training Institute’s typical hours of operation will be
8:30 AM to 3:00 PM, Monday through Friday. There will be a maximum of 15 students per
class/session and one (1) instructor on site at any given time. No tenant improvements or exterior
improvements are proposed.

Parking

The California Legislature has found and declared that the imposition of mandatory parking
minimums can increase the cost of housing, limit the number of available units, lead to an
oversupply of parking spaces, and lead to increased greenhouse gas emissions, therefore, the
Legislature enacted Assembly Bill (AB) 2097, which went into effect as of January 1, 2023. AB
2097 prohibits public agencies from imposing minimum automobile parking requirements for all
projects (residential and commercial) within a half-mile radius of a major transit stop. This proposal
is located within a Transit Priority Area and within a half-mile radius of a major transit stop located
at the intersection of Valley Boulevard and Atlantic Boulevard, and therefore, minimum parking
requirements cannot be enforced for this project and no additional parking is required.

The parking requirements outlined in AMC Section 23.20.040 [Required Parking Spaces] are
based on uses and floor area. The total parking required and provided for the site and all existing
commercial tenants is 53 spaces. Based on the minimum parking ratio requirements for Colleges
and Trade Schools uses, a total of six (6) spaces are required for the proposed use. The
commercial plaza provides 58 off-street parking spaces. Thus, the site provides sufficient parking
for all existing uses and the subject proposed use.
